scenes.title: tensor — one element, one lattice
scenes.description: A 6×6 row-stochastic matrix as a single `tensor` element, beside a static causal mask.
scenes.markdown:
# `tensor`

Both grids below are **one element each**, not 36.

**Left** is live: one `valueExpr`, evaluated per cell with `row` and `col` bound.
Row $i$ is a softmax over $s_{ij} = e^{-|i-j|\cdot k}$, so every row sums to 1. Drag **sharpness** and watch it go from uniform to near-diagonal.

**Right** is static: literal `values`, built once, **zero** per-frame cost — a causal mask, which is exactly the shape that makes parallel training legal.

Cell geometry is arithmetic on `shape`, not expressions, so nothing is re-evaluated for positions that never move.

views.description: The live matrix and the static mask together

steps.title: One element per lattice
steps.description: Drag **sharpness** $k$: at $k=0$ every row is uniform ($1/6$ each); as $k$ grows the mass collapses onto the diagonal. The mask on the right never changes, and costs nothing per frame.

add.valueExpr: (exp(-abs(row - col) * sharp)) / (exp(-abs(row - 0) * sharp) + exp(-abs(row - 1) * sharp) + exp(-abs(row - 2) * sharp) + exp(-abs(row - 3) * sharp) + exp(-abs(row - 4) * sharp) + exp(-abs(row - 5) * sharp))
add.label: softmax rows
add.prompt: This is a row-stochastic attention-style matrix. Each row is a softmax over scores that decay with distance from the diagonal. Explain why every row sums to 1 and what the sharpness slider is doing to the distribution.

add.label: causal mask
add.prompt: This is a causal mask: cell (i,j) is 1 when j <= i. Explain why masking the future is what makes it legal to train on every position of a sequence in a single parallel forward pass.

info.content:
Row 0 sums to $1.000$ by construction.

$\alpha_{00} = {{ (exp(0) / (exp(0) + exp(-1*sharp) + exp(-2*sharp) + exp(-3*sharp) + exp(-4*sharp) + exp(-5*sharp))) }}$
